summary: Backend-only E2E verification of the THIRD LLM provider swap in this session: Gemini(gemini-3.5-flash, quota-exhausted) -> Anthropic(claude-haiku-5-5), using the real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY already present in backend/.env (no mocks). Created /app/backend/tests/test_claude_haiku_provider_switch.py (sequential, fresh TEST_claude_<uuid> user) covering the FULL realistic journey: register -> profile -> recommendations generate+poll -> career detail (fresh+cached) -> custom roadmap ('elektryk') generate+poll -> task resources (fresh+cached) -> daily-plan settings+generate -> premium subscribe + study-plan. ALL 7 tests PASSED (195.7s total). Backend logs for the exact test window (00:37:35-00:42:13 UTC) show zero tracebacks, zero 401/403/429/quota errors, and zero 'No JSON in LLM response' ValueErrors -- every ask_llm() call logged 'model= claude-haiku-5-5; provider = anthropic' cleanly. The regex-based JSON extraction (re.search(r'\{.*\}', text, re.S)) correctly parsed every Claude response (recommendations summary+now/future lists, career detail fields, roadmap milestones/tasks, task resources overview/steps, daily-plan items), so markdown-fence-wrapped JSON (if any) did not break parsing. This is a CLEAN PASS -- no provider-related errors anywhere in the full flow.

minor.issue: No retry/backoff and no distinction surfaced to the user between a transient 429/quota error vs. a genuine parsing failure -- both end up as a generic status:'error' with the raw exception string. Not exercised in this run (no errors occurred), but still a standing design gap carried over from the previous Gemini review (iteration_32) that applies equally to the Anthropic path.

action_items: None blocking. Claude (claude-haiku-5-5) switch is production-ready based on this full E2E pass -- auth to Anthropic works (no 401/403), no rate-limit/quota errors (no 429) were hit across the whole flow (profile, recommendations, career detail x2, custom roadmap, task resources x2, daily-plan settings+generate, premium subscribe + study-plan = ~10+ real LLM calls), and the existing regex JSON extraction in ask_llm() is compatible with Claude's output format.

Low priority / carried over from iteration_32: consider adding a friendlier Polish user-facing message for 429/rate-limit vs. generic parse-error cases in ask_llm()/run_roadmap() error handling, since this failure mode has now been hit twice with other providers (OpenAI->Gemini free tier) in this session.

No visibility into Anthropic's own rate-limit tier for this key from this single-run test; if concurrent/multi-user load is a concern, verify the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY's requests-per-minute/day limits via the Anthropic console before declaring full production readiness at scale (this single-session test only confirms correctness, not sustained throughput).
